name: Leslie 122 Rotor Amplifier and Dividing Network
description: The 122 rotor (main) amplifier and its dividing network, from the 1971 Electro Music factory manual (schematic pages 19-20, parts list page 20) and the 1995 redraw (122mn-a.pdf, Rev 1.1). A 12AU7 differential input stage (V2A/V2B, 56 kOhm plate loads from a 260 V rail, 1.2 kOhm shared cathode, 6 VDC), capacitor-coupled (0.1 uF) into two 6550s in push-pull with 220 kOhm grid leaks, 390 kOhm + 0.0047 uF plate-to-grid feedback around each valve, a 150 Ohm 10 W shared cathode resistor bypassed by 200 uF (25 VDC), 310 VDC screens from a 0C3 series regulator (105 V) behind 470 Ohm, 420 VDC plates from a 430 VDC bridge reservoir through a choke. Output transformer into the double-section m-derived dividing network at 800 Hz: series 7.8 uF with the treble driver shunted by 3.2 mH, and series 5.2 mH into the 15-inch bass driver shunted by 12.5 uF; both drivers 16 Ohm. The rotors are NOT part of this netlist: io.output carries the treble (horn) band voltage and io.outputR the bass (drum) band voltage, both speaker-level, for the rotary model.

sources.title: Electro Music/CBS, 'Leslie Speakers 122, 122V, 122RV, 142, 222, 222RV', installation/operating/maintenance manual 044578, June 1971: schematic '117V Type 122 Rotor and Reverb Amplifiers' (printed pp. 19-20), parts list 'Type 122 Rotor Amplifier' (printed p. 20), SPECIFICATIONS and 'Rotor, Speaker, Dividing Network Servicing' (800 Hz, 16 Ohm drivers, 40 W, 190 W consumption), volume-control setting procedure (p. 6)
1995 redraw of the same schematic, '117V Type 122 Rotor and Reverb Amplifiers', Rev 1.1, Oct 25 1995 (vector; every value cited by crop coordinate)

Leslie 122 dividing-network and driver impedances: the 1971 manual, 'Both of these loudspeakers are of the permanent magnet type with 16 ohm impedances'; 'A double section, M-derived frequency Dividing Network separates signal output from the rotor amp into frequencies above and below 800 Hz'

io.note: Balanced input on P1 pins 1/6, driven differentially (input and its inverted copy). io.output = 'horn' (treble band, the voltage across the compression driver) and io.outputR = 'd1' (bass band, across the 15-inch driver). outputVoltsPerFS 46 = 1.5 x the larger dimed peak (horn 30.5 Vpk at 3 kHz; drum 28.0 Vpk at 220 Hz; volume 1). inputVoltsPerFS 3.0 V peak is the differential input that reaches full output at volume 1.

controls.label: Volume
controls.note: R2, the ROTOR AMP volume control (100 kOhm audio taper) across the two 10 kOhm input legs. 0 = the input legs are shorted (silent); 1 = the pad is out. The manual sets it just below distortion with full organ (page 6). This is the amplifier's only control; the catalogue's 15 parameters are rotor-model parameters and are legacyOnly here.

parts.note: The 310 VDC screen rail, as drawn: 420 V -(R17 470 Ohm)-(V5 0C3, 105 V)- 310 V, with C5B 30 uF. The engine has no gas-tube device and a 105 V zener stand-in is bistable in this series position: the DC solve stays on the branch with the 6550 screens at 405 V (above the plates), the grids at +5.4 V and 111 mA/tube for ~200 ms after reset, instead of the drawn 310 V / 25 V point. A VR tube holds 105 V +/- 1 V over 5-30 mA, i.e. the rail is a voltage source; C5B (30 uF) and the tube's ~100 Ohm slope make it an AC ground, so this fixed rail keeps the drawn operating point, the DC and the AC. Given up: R17's ~5 V drop and the rail's tracking of the 420 V supply's sag; R17 is therefore not fitted (against 310 V it would draw 230 mA from the 420 V rail).
parts.label: 310 VDC screens (0C3 regulated)

parts.note: The 0C3's dynamic (slope) resistance, ~80 Ohm from the datasheet's 2 V regulation over 5-30 mA; with the rail modelled as a 310 V source this is the tube's only remaining series element.
C5B 30 uF 475 V: screen-rail decoupling (the 1971 sheet marks this section C5B too)
parts.label: 310 V screens

parts.note: R2 (parts list 055186, 'Potentiometer, 100K, Audio Taper') is wired as a rheostat across the two 10 kOhm input legs: the wiper and the CCW end both land on C8's node, so the resistance na..n2 runs 0..100 kOhm with the taper. FITTED: 4.3 kOhm plate-to-plate (6550 pair at 420 V plates / 310 V screens, 40 W rating) and an 8 Ohm secondary, whose two drawn halves are paralleled about an earthed centre tap (x=541.9 y=282.5 is the ground symbol; the two ends are tied at x=550.4). parts.label: Balanced-drive glue
parts.note: The 122 input is a balanced pair on P1 pins 1 and 6 (the organ's Leslie output is balanced; the amp's own return leg R3 goes through 10 kOhm and is not grounded). The engine drives one input node, so this unity inverting VCVS makes the second leg. No hardware part; it is the interface.
L2 3.2 mH choke (dividing network 052803): shunt across the treble driver

parts.label: Treble driver 16 Ohm

Horn band readout
parts.note: The treble driver's voice coil is between the amp hot node (cx) and L2's far end (h2). This unity VCVS exports that difference so the rotor model can read the treble band single-ended. Interface glue.
